title: Fights on the boats and the Piron band's final season
summary: Trouble among passengers, police on board, dissension in Piron's band, and pay.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: What was it like playing on the boats? I mean, from what I heard, you know, I heard like one thing there were a lot of fights on the boats.

At times there were. Yeah, that would be a, you see what happened, not much here. But those, St. Louis I know, a lot of those people up there, St. Louis you have what you call those, what's it called, the Irish, because they had two boats. One was a cheap boat and one was a high. They didn't have much on the boats that we were going on. They had another boat there, I can't think of it, in the Ammoor. They would fight among themselves. And they had one night, they had for color. They requested that the Catholic, but they had a lot of fun out there, the second, a few more people were Catholic. And yeah, it was St. Paul, that's what it was, I believe. But not so much on the first class boat, because if the fights they had to play, you know, those kind of people couldn't afford that. That's what I'm talking about, you see. And once in a while they had them on air, not too much air, but they always had enough sufficient support to break that up, you see. Break that up. But when we'd be a tramp, I call it tramp, down the river, you play in those different town, they'd have different group of fights, you know, but they'd get that straight in the

They'd change that out, but they had enough help, or they had enough guys, but if there wasn't police, then most of the time they'd have to hire police in each city you go in, to be on the boat. I see. I see how they did that, you see. And they had a little small, and they had two smalls, you know, put them in. Sometimes they'd just line them up somewhere and put them somewhere until the boat would come back off its trip, moonlight trip, or something like that. Yeah. It's not a little while. Okay. That's where we lived there, in the other place? Versace. Versace. Versace. Versace, I know, yeah. Now, where were we at? We were talking about the steamboats. The steamboats. The excursion boats. Yeah, the excursion boats, yeah. So, yeah, I did see a way. So, I think, yeah, the part where Puron didn't go in 48, we had worked at a place on Bourbon Street there, and I think it was, oh, let's see, one, two, three, four, one, three, four blocks from, three or four blocks from Canal Street. And we got that job doing the holidays. And the man took a ride in the Puron, and he had a lady doing a partner slip thing, beautiful lady. And we were told to keep very good manners and everything. And it lasted until, yeah, you know, we played a little over the holidays. But we went through three nights. And when time the boat comes, people only didn't want to go. Captain Aldrich, and we were working at the New Orleans Country Club here on Sunday. Thought we might have been Friday and Saturday on Sunday. So, he called us out, drawn to the boat. Peter on board Peter Bookerage. And he really scoved Peter on out. I knew where it was going. I don't know if the other of them were going to drop. So, Peter on stayed on the job and took it to small pieces, about three or four pieces to work. And he said, well, it was something that helped. That's what he said. Yeah. Well, that's what it was, yeah. Because if you don't suffer with that thing that people can't hear, right? Ashton or something like that, they get up in that part of the country, it's better for them. Oh, yeah. It could be something like asthma. It's up close to asthma or something like that. I've seen them. It's something come from the trees that are in front of the flowers. Oh, yeah. Pollen or something, they call it, yeah. And when you get up in that area, it didn't have that. And here a few of you had something that didn't happen. So, that was his excuse, you see. So, that's how Peter Bookerage got in the band, because I'm repeating myself, you see. And then, like I told you, after when we got through September, I knew I could see the band wasn't going to last long. And we had a really good band. Well, you had to be good to be on the stretcher's team. Yeah. There wasn't a hire. I mean, if they did, but hire, they let you go. So, when you work that whole season, and work the next year and things, you had to be good. Then you had to have a special orshery. You go in the boat and let the captain listen at the band before he signed the contract to hire you. And I worked with Faith Marver. That was $35 the most money I ever made in my life. That was a lot of money in those days. Well, they did drop it down, the pressure dropped it down to $25, I believe. Which still wasn't too bad, because you had nothing to do. The only thing you had to pay for was to keep your clothes washed. You could wash your own clothes if you want, or whatever someone did. But they had to sit and stop, they'd tell you, well, it's going to be a laundry. For instance, they'd get in the place where they're going to pray, and two days or three days, they'll tell you. The laundry will be there. There's money coming, and pick your laundry, and bring it back the same day. And you could do some of your own washing if you want.
